`concat`, `reduce` and `flatMap(x => x)` can all flatten an array of arrays, but a reader has to work out that this is what they do. `.flat()` says it.

`--fix` rewrites the `flatMap` and `reduce` forms to `.flat()`. `--fix-dangerously` also rewrites `[].concat.apply([], array)`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 5} */}
```js
const a = pages.flatMap(items => items);
const b = pages.reduce((all, items) => all.concat(items), []);
const c = pages.reduce((all, items) => [...all, ...items], []);
const d = [].concat(...pages);
const e = [].concat.apply([], pages);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const items = pages.flat();
```

A `flatMap` that changes the elements is not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const tags = posts.flatMap(post => post.tags);
```
